prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. PRODUCTION REFERENCE SHEET, landscape, not a finished book page. Bold clean clear 2D children's cartoon throughout, crisp continuous dark outlines, flat clean colors, restrained smooth cel shading, no painted or grainy texture, no gouache, no embossed relief, no 3D. Original friendly readable illustration. Ordinary neutral settings; no flags, religious/political symbols or costumes. No logos, text, letters, numbers, pseudo-writing, captions, watermarks or page borders. Natural anatomy and coherent hand/prop contact. Essential content at least 8 percent inside every edge.
WD-KIT / Kit: six-year-old human boy, golden light-medium skin, short straight black side-parted hair, teal T-shirt, mustard shorts, navy sneakers. WD-ZOE / Zoe: six-year-old human girl, deep brown skin, black hair in two puffs, yellow T-shirt, plum overalls, white sneakers. Kit and Zoe have equal standing height. Include only characters needed by this exact scene, not every reference pose. Preserve exact reference identity and clothing.
Book: The Stretchy Bridge; World Discovery; fiction.
Setting: World Discovery classroom play table in afternoon light. A narrow blue cloth river separates two tan cardboard banks; a small red toy garage stands on the far bank with its hinged door facing the river.
Design locks for the book's recurring subjects/props (NOT a visibility list; never insert later objects/states prematurely): One teal wooden-looking magic toy bridge with low side rails; One yellow four-wheeled toy truck; One red toy garage with hinged door; One fixed blue cloth river and two flat tan cardboard banks
 Create a clean separated reference board on white: show the principal recurring props/animals in front, side and three-quarter views, their relative scale beside any named human cast, and a single simple location key showing the persistent setting and daylight/palette. The human character model sheet is a supporting identity reference, not content to copy wholesale. Show only the subjects this book requires. Use initial object states: One bridge; initial short length; width and rails fixed.. For orientation, the opening location/action is: World Discovery classroom play table in afternoon light. A narrow blue cloth river separates two tan cardboard banks; a small red toy garage stands on the far bank with its hinged door facing the river. Zoe holds the teal toy bridge beside Kit’s tabletop river and garage, ready to demonstrate; it is currently short. Exact state: One bridge; initial short length; width and rails fixed.. Do not show a completed craft or later scene merely because the finished object is listed in design locks. No future story events, no captions.

visualReview.note: Reference inspected: short teal toy bridge with side rails, yellow four-wheel truck, red garage with left-hinged door, blue cloth river and tan cardboard banks. Bridge is held short before use; toy scale and cast match. No later crossing or completed solution shown.
visualReview.limits: Direct agent visual review; no classroom or physical-device observation.
